rv.q: Unfortunately, Mr. Mann has shoehorned them into a cartoonishly corny story.
All of them will be recognized by Deadheads and appreciated by others, although some may have a headache halfway through the show.

Though it’s wonderful experiencing such spirited renditions of Grateful Dead classics such as “Truckin,” “Casey Jones,” “Alabama Getaway” and “A Touch of Grey” by the talented ensemble, Red Roses, Green Gold doesn’t really cohere into a satisfying work of musical theater.
Whether it's worth wading through a drawn-out plot to get to those performances will depend on how invested you are in the music.
Red Roses, Green Gold is an entertaining reimagining of the nostalgic and transportive music of the Grateful Dead, in a new theatrical context and style.
Red Roses Green Gold may not make into the pantheon of rock musicals, but when the music plays, it will certainly provide you with a good time and make you feel gratefully alive.
There are wonderful songs...The music is admirably performed...and a storyline so poorly conceived and executed that it almost ruins the fun.
In short, you might have a perfectly good time at 'Red Roses, Green Gold,' even if it's less a diamond in the rough and more fool's gold.
